products.summary: The L3600 is the cheapest lithium power station sold in the US with a built-in wind input. It pairs a 3,072 Wh LiFePO4 battery and a 3,600 W inverter with up to 2,400 W of solar and a 150 W port for the maker's own turbine, so a cabin or a home's essential circuits can charge from both sources without a separate charge controller.
products.fit: Cabin, homestead or home-backup buyers who want solar plus a wind top-up at night, 120 V loads only, and room to add Power Pods later.
caveats: Wind adds at most 150 W, and only in a 27 mph wind; at a 10 mph site expect a few watts, so size the solar for the real load.
The wind turbine, its adapter and a mounting pole are sold separately.
120 V output only; a 240 V well pump or dryer needs the L6000 or MyGrid 10K.
Warranty is 1 year, against 5 years on BLUETTI's Elite 200 V2.
Weight is not listed on the store page; a retailer spec sheet shows about 97 lb, so plan on two people or the maker's cart.

specs: Up to 150 W at about 27 mph
Controller box, 100 ft wind-rated cable, hub, hardware
L3600 and L6000 (adapter required), Elite 3600, Standard 1800
Cast aluminum alloy, powder-coated; fiberglass nylon blades
products.warranty: 1-year limited warranty; register the unit with Nature's Generator.
products.returns: 30 days from delivery on direct store orders; RMA number required; 15% restocking fee if not in original condition; return shipping deducted unless the product is defective or arrived damaged.
products.summary: The only turbine that plugs straight into a Nature's Generator power station. It comes with its controller, hub and 100 ft of cable; you supply the pole and a site with steady wind.
products.fit: Owners of an L3600, L6000, Elite 3600 or Standard 1800 on a windy, open site who want charging to continue after dark.
caveats: Rated at 27 mph; the Department of Energy's small-wind handbook puts the useful floor at a 9 mph annual average, and output falls with the cube of wind speed.
Needs a pole that puts the rotor 30 ft above anything within 300 ft; none is included.
Three owner reports (two Tractor Supply reviews, one BBB complaint) describe turbines that arrived damaged or produced nothing; test it inside the 30-day window.

products.summary: The L6000 is the cheapest 240 V split-phase power station with a wind input. Its 6,000 W inverter runs a well pump or central-air circuit through a transfer switch, and it stacks up to five pods for multi-day outages.
products.fit: Whole-home or well-pump backup where 240 V matters, with solar as the main charge source and wind as a top-up.
caveats: Same 150 W wind ceiling as the L3600; the 350 W turbine is for the MyGrid 10K only.
112 lb and no built-in wheels; the maker's cart is a separate purchase.
A 240 V transfer switch and installation are extra.
